entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Chandan Agarwal,Neeraj Dube
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Donadi Ramesh,J.
1.

The instant petition has been filed praying for quashing of the order dated 23.11.2022 passed by respondent no.3 i.e Special Land Acquisition Officer, Bijnor rejecting the request of the petitioner for release of compensation amount in his favour in lieu of acquisition of his land bearing khasra no.
422M.
2.
It is not in dispute that the aforesaid khasra number was duly notified for acquisition under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956.
An award was also passed for the acquired land.

When the petitioner applied for release of compensation, the respondents by impugned order rejected his request for release of compensation amount on the ground that as per report of Fazaluddin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149432173/
1 Tehsildar Najibabad and opinion of D.G.C., the petitioner could not have acquired bhumidhari rights on the said land having regard to Section 77 of U.P. Revenue Code, 2006.

entities.text: Fazaluddin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that title of the petitioner was decided after long drawn contest in the past.
The order of the Board of Revenue passed in this behalf dated 18.10.2021 has attained finality as it was not challenged by the State nor by the Gaon Sabha.
The said order declares the petitioner-Fazaluddin as one of the bhumidhars of the aforesaid land.
Merely on basis of report of Tehsildar and opinion of D.G.C., the claim of the petitioner could not have been rejected.
4. The respondents have furnished instructions to the State counsel, the same is taken on record.

It is not disputed therein that the order of the Board of Revenue dated 21.05.2019 declaring the petitioner as one of the bhumidhars of the land in question, is still in subsistence and continues to govern the rights of the parties in the subject land.
Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing counsel submits that the State intends to challenge the aforesaid order.
However, the fact remains that the said order has still not been set aside by any court.
5. The report of Tehsildar or opinion of D.G.C. cannot be made basis to sit over the order of Board of Revenue passed on merits after contest between the petitioner and the State.
6. We are of the considered opinion that the impugned order dated 23.11.2022 is manifestly illegal and is, accordingly, quashed.
Matter is remitted back to respondent no.3 for passing a fresh order, in accordance with law, within a period of eight weeks from the date of communication of this order.
(Donadi Ramesh, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 10.8.2023
